name: Utility Belt
summary: The yellow belt that lets Batman pull out exactly the right gadget at exactly the wrong moment for his enemies. Its capsules became pouches, and its rope became a grapple gun.

parts.label: Buckle
parts.fact: Most versions hide a miniature camera and a tape recorder behind the bat-emblem buckle, turning the belt into a portable evidence kit.

parts.label: Gas capsules
parts.fact: In its first appearance, Detective Comics #29 (1939), the belt carried capsules of choking gas. Comics historian Les Daniels credits the idea to writer Gardner Fox.

parts.label: Rebreather
parts.fact: A compact rebreather rides in one pouch and holds about two and a half minutes of air, enough for an underwater escape or a gas-filled room.

parts.label: Anti-tamper
parts.fact: Snatching the belt is a bad idea: in the comics it can shock whoever grabs it or puff stun gas in their face. In Batman: Year One a stray thermite charge burns it up.

parts.label: Grapple line
parts.fact: On film, Tim Burton's Batman (1989) debuted a handheld grapple gun; the comics adopted one in Batman #458 (1991), drawn by Norm Breyfogle.

trivia: The batarang showed up just two issues after the belt, in Detective Comics #31 (1939).
For decades artists drew simple capsules on the belt; Frank Miller's The Dark Knight Returns (1986) switched to military-style pouches, which became standard by 2000.
Famous mix-up: in the 1966 Batman film the shark-repellent spray is not on the belt at all; Robin passes it down from the Batcopter.
Batman Returns (1992) added a tiny motor that slides gadgets from the back of the belt to the front.
